title: Stripe Pricing 2026: Total Transaction & Add-on Costs
summary: Stripe pricing structures involve complex variables that impact your bottom line.
body_markdown:
## Realistic Monthly Costs for Different Transaction Volumes


Plan Name Monthly Fee Included Volume Transaction Fee (Domestic) Transaction Fee (International) Manually Entered Surcharge


Integrated $0 None 2.9% + 30¢ 4.4% + 30¢ +0.5%


Standard $0 None 2.9% + 30¢ 4.4% + 30¢ +0.5%


*Prices and plan limits checked against[stripe.com](https://stripe.com/pricing) on September 30, 2026.*


Stripe's Standard plan applies the same 2.9% + 30¢ domestic rate regardless of volume, so there is no $500 monthly fixed overhead to budget for.


### Understanding the Scale plan volume credit


Stripe's Standard plan has no monthly platform fee — it charges 2.9% + 30¢ per successful domestic transaction regardless of volume.


There is no included-volume credit on Stripe's Standard plan; every domestic transaction is charged the same 2.9% + 30¢ rate regardless of monthly volume.


> The $500 monthly fee for the Scale plan functions as a minimum platform spend rather than a pure subscription tax.


There is no volume threshold at which a lower 2.7% rate kicks in — Stripe's Standard plan charges 2.9% + 30¢ per successful domestic transaction at any volume.


### Calculating the volume break-even point


Stripe does not offer a discounted Scale tier with a lower volume rate or fixed transaction fee, so there is no $250,000 break-even point to calculate.


Because Stripe's Standard plan has no per-transaction discount or monthly fee to recover, this break-even calculation doesn't apply.


Since Stripe charges the same 2.9% + 30¢ rate regardless of order value or volume, there's no subscription cost to justify.


Stripe's Standard plan charges the same 2.9% + 30¢ domestic rate at every volume level, so there is no break-even threshold to reach.


What follows is a breakdown of how these rates manifest across three specific business stages.


### The Startup Scenario: $50k Monthly Volume


For a startup processing $50,000 a month, the "standard" rate is a myth because the transaction mix is rarely 100% domestic credit cards.


At this stage, your effective rate for a standard[Domestic Card](https://stripe.com/pricing) is 3.2%, which means nearly a third of every dollar earned is being diverted away from your core operations.


If you're selling software to a global audience, the[International Card](https://stripe.com/pricing) rate jumps to 4.7%. A single $100 subscription from a UK customer only nets you $95.30, forcing you to absorb the hidden costs of international commerce directly from your revenue.


If a customer chooses[Klarna US](https://stripe.com/pricing) , the fee hits 6.0%. You pay $3,000 in fees on just $50,000 of volume, which is a heavy price for a small team trying to maintain a 20% net margin.


### The Mid-Market Scenario: $500k Monthly Volume


At $500,000 in monthly volume, the complexity of currency conversion becomes a primary drain on the bottom line, making financial forecasting an exercise in guesswork rather than strategy, which means leadership is effectively flying blind when setting annual growth targets.


When an[Intl. with FX](https://stripe.com/pricing) transaction occurs, the rate climbs to 5.4%, which means your profitability on international sales is being eroded by more than double the standard domestic fee.


Teams at this scale use[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) to automate the sync of Stripe metadata to internal databases, ensuring the run is the meter rather than the steps inside it.


Pricing that scales with granularity penalizes the exact discipline reliable automation requires (breaking work into smaller, more resilient steps) so it effectively taxes a builder for doing the job properly.


By billing one credit per flow run regardless of complexity, as shown on their published pricing page, the platform ensures that adding a reconciliation step to a payment flow doesn't increase the cost of the automation itself.


Businesses must prioritize localized payment methods to avoid these steep penalties.


Until then, the 5.4% rate acts as a border tax that eats into the budget for two mid-level engineering hires every single month, so the company is forced to choose between scaling its product and paying for its payment infrastructure.


Even at Stripe's standard 2.9% + 30¢ domestic rate, the manual entry of credit cards over the phone adds a 0.5% surcharge, meaning every customer service interaction carries an invisible penalty that accumulates with every call.


A sales team manually closing $50,000 of that volume is effectively burning an extra $250 on avoidable administrative friction, so the business is essentially paying a premium for inefficient manual labor.


### The Enterprise Scenario: $5M+ Monthly Volume


Enterprise users processing $5M or more monthly aren't looking at individual transaction fees anymore, which means they have shifted their focus toward high-level liquidity and long-term capital efficiency. The focus shifts from per-swipe costs to holistic operational overhead.


At this scale, even a 0.1% difference in the effective rate represents $5,000 a month, enough to fund a dedicated DevOps resource, meaning that small optimization gains translate directly into significant headcount capacity.


Regulated organizations at this volume often require the same level of control over their automation as they do their payments.


The enterprise feature list (including SSO, SCIM, and custom RBAC) in the Activepieces self-hosted air-gapped docs matches the managed cloud exactly, allowing companies to bridge Stripe events to internal systems without sacrificing governance.


Public-sector entities run this air-gapped edition in production today to maintain strict data residency while automating high-volume financial workflows.


While these companies negotiate custom contracts, they're still subject to the 6.0% Klarna US rate unless they have the leverage to bring their own credit terms, so they remain vulnerable to significant margin erosion on every high-ticket purchase.


The goal at $5M+ is to drive the blended rate back toward 3% by aggressively routing domestic traffic through cheaper rails, which means scaling operations requires a sophisticated approach to transaction pathing.


Staying at the 4.7% international average would result in $235,000 in monthly fees, a cost that often triggers a board-level review of alternative processors, so finance teams must weigh the stability of current providers against the potential for significant savings.
